A DAR was filed on 11.04.2019 by Investigation Officer (IO), HC Ashok Kumar before this Tribunal in the presence of all the parties of this case.

The DAR was prepared by IO in respect of a motor vehicular accident which occurred on 03.04.2018, at about 05:15 P.M. near Bus Terminal Park, P-4 Block, Sultanpuri, Delhi in which two girls Baby Aayat and Baby Mahira sustained injuries.
The present DAR has been filed on behalf of Baby Mahira through her father (hereinafter referred to as "petitioner").
As per FIR, one Ramzan, uncle of the petitioner is the eye- witness of the accident who had stated that on 3.04.2018 at about 5:15 PM, two daughters of his younger brother were playing in the Park.

sentences.text: 1 respondent no. 1/ driver (herein after referred to as "R-1") in rash and negligent manner, and in high speed entered into service road.
R-1 turned the offending vehicle in the gate of the park.
Both the daughters were hit by the car and over-run by the rear wheel of the car.
He made call at number 100.
R-1 was apprehended on the spot with the help of public persons.
Petitioner was taken to Sanjay Gandhi Memorial Hospital where her MLC No. 5130 was prepared wherein doctor opined that the injuries sustained by the petitioner are simple in nature.
An FIR no. 243/18, U/s 279/337 IPC was registered at PS Sultanpuri.
Respondent no. 2 is the owner of the offending vehicle.
Offending vehicle was not insured at the time of accident.

2. The respondents failed to file the written statement despite opportunities and finally vide order dated 02.08.2019, their right to file the MACT Case No. 194/19 (FIR no. 243/2018) Baby Mahira v.
Bharat & Ors.
Page no. 2 of 9 written statement was closed and they were also proceeded ex-parte.
Therefore, no issues were framed.
PETITIONER'S EVIDENCE 3.

The petitioner has examined Sh. Ramzan as PW-1 who filed his evidence by way of affidavit Ex.
PW1/A and relied upon the DAR Ex. PW 1/1.
He reiterated the facts mentioned in the FIR.

Petitioner has also examined her mother Sakina as PW-2 who filed her evidence by way of affidavit Ex. P2. PW-2 relied upon copy of her Aadhar Card Ex PW 2/1 and Report card of petitioner Ex. PW 2/2.
4. PW1 was cross-examined in brief on behalf of R-3 wherein he submitted that he does not have any proof that he has incurred Rs. 1,50,000/- with regard to treatment, conveyance and attendant charges.
He further stated that he has not placed any medical bills of treatment on record.
5. No evidence was lead in defence by the respondents.
FINDINGS 6.
Oral submissions were advanced on behalf of the petitioner by Ms. Surender Kaur, Advocate.
I have gone through the record.

7. It is well settled that the procedure followed for proceedings conducted by an accident tribunal is similar to that followed by a civil court and in civil matters the facts are required to be established by preponderance of probabilities only and not by strict rules of evidence or beyond reasonable doubts as are required in a criminal prosecution.
The MACT Case No. 194/19 (FIR no. 243/2018) Baby Mahira v. Bharat & Ors.

Page no. 3 of 9 burden of proof in a civil case is never as heavy as that is required in a criminal case,
but in a claim petition under the Motor Vehicles Act, this burden is infact even lesser than that in a civil case.

sentences.text: As already discussed above, the petitioner examined PW-1 in order to prove the factual averments regarding the occurrence of accident.

PW-1 has clearly and categorically stated that on 03.04.2018,
at about 5:15 PM, daughters aged about 5 years and 1 year, of his brother Imtiaz Ahmed were playing at the gate of park in front of the house at the relevant date, time and place, they were hit by the offending vehicle, which was being driven by R-1 at a high speed and in a rash and negligent manner and it over run the petitioner and her sister by its rear wheel.
He further deposed that petitioner sustained injuries due to the said overrun by the offending vehicle.
His testimony remained unrebutted as he was not cross-examined by the respondents being ex-parte.
As such, this Tribunal finds it appropriate to hold that the oral testimony of PW-1 is reliable and trustworthy.

9. The very fact that R-1 has already been charge-sheeted for the offences punishable under Sections 279/337/338 IPC in the above criminal case/FIR in itself is a strong circumstance to support the above oral testimony of PW-1 and the case of petitioners on this issue.

The copies of MACT Case No.
194/19 (FIR no. 243/2018) Baby Mahira v. Bharat & Ors.
Page no. 4 of 9 FIR, Charge-sheet, Site plan, Mechanical inspection report of offending vehicle, MLC also corroborate the oral testimony of PW-1.
10.

Besides the above, R-1 himself was the best witness who could have stepped into the witness box to challenge the depositions being made by PW-1 regarding the above accident and its manner etc.,
but he has not done so.

Therefore, an adverse inference on this aspect is also required to be drawn against the respondents in view of the law laid down in case of Cholamandalam M.S. General Insurance Company Ltd. Vs. Kamlesh, reported in 2009 (3) AD (Delhi) 310.
11.

entities.text: Cholamandalam M.S. General Insurance Company Ltd. Vs. Kamlesh, reported in 2009 (3) AD (Delhi) 310
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In view of the above discussion, this tribunal is constrained to hold R-1 guilty of gross neglect and default in riding the offending vehicle at the relevant time.
In view of the medical treatment documents placed on record on behalf of the petitioner, no dispute is left regarding the nature of injuries sustained by her in the above accident.

12. In view of the above discussion, this Tribunal holds that the petitioner suffered simple injuries on her person on account of neglect and default of R-1 while driving the offending vehicle at the relevant time.
13. The petitioner has become entitled to be compensated for the injuries suffered in the above accident, but the computation of compensation and liability to pay the same are required to be decided.

sentences.text: In terms of provisions contained in Section 168 of the MV Act the compensation which is to be awarded by this tribunal is required to be 'just'.
In the injury cases a claimant is entitled to two different kinds of compensations i.e. pecuniary as well as non-pecuniary damages.
The MACT Case No. 194/19 (FIR no. 243/2018) Baby Mahira v. Bharat & Ors.
Page no. 5 of 9

pecuniary damages or special damages are those damages which are awarded and designed to make good the losses which are capable of being calculated in terms of money and the object of awarding these damages is to indemnify the claimant for the expenses which she had already incurred or is likely to incur in respect of the injuries suffered by her in the accident.

The non-pecuniary or general damages are those damages which are incapable of being assessed which includes the compensation for the mental or physical shock, pain and sufferings, loss of amenities of life and disfiguration etc.
The above categories falling under both the heads of compensation are not exhaustive in nature but only illustrative.

It is also necessary to state here that no amount of money or compensation can put the injured/claimant exactly in the same position or place where she was before the accident and an effort is to be made only to reasonably compensate her or to put her almost in the same place or position where she could have been if the alleged accident had not taken place and this compensation is to be assessed in a fair, reasonable and equitable manner.

Reference in this regard can be made on some of important judgments on the subject like the judgment in the case of Raj Kumar Vs. Ajay Kumar & Anr., (2011) 1 SCC 343.
15.

Medical or Treatment Expenses:
16. PW-1 has deposed after the accident, petitioner was taken to Sanjay Gandhi Memorial Hospital,
Rohini, Delhi.

entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: Petitioner was diagnosed with fracture of right Femur vide MLC no. 5133/2018.

But,
no medical documents/ bills have been placed on record to prove that how much MACT Case No.
194/19 (FIR no. 243/2018) Baby Mahira v. Bharat & Ors.
Page no. 6 of 9 money was incurred by the parents of petitioner for her treatment.
Therefore, the petitioner is granted a nominal amount of Rs. 10,000/ under this head.

Pain and Suffering:
17.
As per the MLC bearing no. 5133/2018, the petitioner sustained fracture on right Femur in the above accident.
As per MLC, the age of petitioner was only one year at the time of accident.

It is not possible to quantify the compensation admissible to petitioner for the shock, pain and sufferings etc.
which she actually suffered because of the above injuries, but as stated above, an effort has to be made to compensate her for the same in a just and reasonable manner.

Hence, keeping in view the extent and nature of the injuries suffered by petitioner and duration of the treatment taken by her etc., an amount of Rs. 50,000/ is being awarded to her towards pain and sufferings during the said period of his treatment and immobility.
Thus, she is awarded a total amount of Rs. 50,000/ under this head.

4 Loss of actual earnings:
18.

As per the material placed on judicial file by the petitioner i.e. MLC No. 5133 dated 03.04.2018,
petitioner had suffered only grievous injuries.
PW-2 deposed that the petitioner remained on bed for one month and due to which she and her husband has suffered financially.
No income certificate has been placed on record in this regard.
Since the petitioner was a minor, therefore, it could be safely assumed that she was accompanied by her parents.
In the facts and circumstances, the minimum wages as applicable in Delhi on the date of accident i.e. 03.04.2018 are taken into account for calculation of the compensation under this head.

Therefore, the MACT Case No. 194/19 (FIR no.
243/2018) Baby Mahira v. Bharat & Ors.
Page no. 7 of 9 petitioner is granted one month's minimum wages i.e. Rs. 13,896/- each for her both parents.
Thus, a sum of Rs. 27,792/- is awarded to the petitioner under this head.
Conveyance and Special Diet 19.
No claim has been made by the petitioner under this head.
However, considering the nature of injuries and the age of the petitioner, she is granted Rs. 40,000/- under this head.
Issue No.3/Relief 20.

The petitioner is thus entitled to a sum of Rs. 1,27,792/- (Rupees One Lakhs Twenty Seven Thousand Seven Hundred and Ninety Two Only) - (Rs. 10,000/- + Rs. 50,000/- + Rs. 27,792/- +
Rs. 40,000/-) along with interest @ 9% per annum from the date of filing of the DAR i.e.
11.04.2019.

However, it is directed that the amount of interim award and interest for the suspended period, if any, during the course of this inquiry, shall be liable to be excluded from the above amount and calculations of compensation.

It has been held that the accident occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle by respondent no.1 and owner of the offending vehicle/R2 are jointly liable to pay the compensation amount.
The offending vehicle was not insured and therefore, R1 and R2 are jointly liable to indemnify the petitioner in respect of above liability.

Respondent no. 1 and 2 are directed to deposit the Award amount in the SBI, Rohini Court Branch within 30 days as per above order,
